A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Inductive Family|inductive family]] $\map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n}$ with constructors:
:$\mathsf {nil} : \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, 0}, \quad \mathsf {cons} : A \to \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n} \to \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n + 1}$
supports a total $\mathsf {head} : \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n + 1} \to A$ and $\mathsf {append} : \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, m} \to \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n} \to \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, m + n}$, and $\sum_{n : \N} \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n} \simeq \map {\mathsf {List} } A$.

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Inductive Type|inductive type]] $\map {\mathsf {List} } A$ has constructors $\mathsf {nil}$ and $\mathsf {cons} : A \to \map {\mathsf {List} } A \to \map {\mathsf {List} } A$, with $\mathsf {append}$ defined by recursion on the first argument; $\mathsf {head}$ has no value at $\mathsf {nil}$.

derived.length in the type: totality of head and the length law for append

object_map.reformulation: Generalize the inductive type to a family indexed by the length, so that the type records an invariant.

validity_conditions: The nil case of head is impossible because 0 and n + 1 are distinct constructors of N.
The type of append matches because m + n is defined by recursion on m, mirroring append.
proof_plan: Index lists by their length, so that each constructor states how it changes the length.
For $\mathsf {head}$, dependent pattern matching on $\map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n + 1}$ only needs the $\mathsf {cons}$ case, as $\mathsf {nil}$ would require $0 = n + 1$.
Define $\mathsf {append}$ by recursion on the first vector, as for lists; the types check because $0 + n \equiv n$ and $\paren {m + 1} + n \equiv \paren {m + n} + 1$.

Forgetting the index, $\tuple {n, v} \mapsto v$ with the index erased gives $\sum_n \map {\mathsf {Vec} } {A, n} \simeq \map {\mathsf {List} } A$, so vectors refine lists.
{{qed}}
